items.followUp: Define acceleration due to gravity and state its direction near Earth’s surface.

rubric.why: The definition must identify gravitational acceleration as the change in velocity per unit time due to gravity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is the rate of change of velocity per unit time due to gravity.

rubric.why: The standard value near Earth’s surface is approximately 9.8 m/s².
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving 9.8 m/s² (or 9.81 m/s²). Direction downward may also be stated.

modelAnswer: Gravitational acceleration is the change in velocity per unit time of a freely falling body due to gravity.
Its value near Earth’s surface is g = 9.8 m/s², directed downward.

items.followUp: A circular track has a radius of 4.0 m. Find the distance covered in half a round.

rubric.why: The radius must be correctly identified from the question.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for writing r = 3.18 m.

rubric.why: Half the circumference is πr, giving approximately 9.99 m.
rubric.description: Uses the half-circumference relation and gives the distance
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct relation and a numerically correct distance with unit.

modelAnswer: Distance in half round = half the circumference = πr

items.followUp: What is plasma, and name two places or phenomena in nature where it is found.

rubric.why: Plasma is an ionized state of matter containing charged particles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as an ionized gas or as a gas containing ions and free electrons.

rubric.why: The Sun and stars are natural examples of plasma; lightning is also an accepted example.
rubric.description: Gives a natural location or example
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a correct natural example, such as the Sun, stars, or lightning.

modelAnswer: Plasma is an ionized gas consisting of positive ions and free electrons.
It exists naturally in the Sun and other stars; lightning is also an example.

items.followUp: Define compressive strain and explain why strain has no unit.

rubric.why: Tensile strain is the ratio of extension to original length.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the ratio of extension (or change in length) to original length.

rubric.why: Both quantities in the ratio are lengths, so their units cancel.
rubric.description: Explains why it has no unit
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the units cancel because the numerator and denominator are both lengths.

modelAnswer: Tensile strain is the ratio of the extension of a body to its original length.
It has no unit because both extension and original length are measured in the same unit, which cancels in the ratio.

items.followUp: Why does an iron nail sink in water while a hollow iron ship can float?

rubric.why: A piece of stone is denser than water and displaces too little water for the upthrust to balance its weight.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the stone’s greater density (or insufficient upthrust) to its sinking.

rubric.why: The ship’s hollow shape gives it a large volume, allowing it to displace enough water for the upthrust to balance its weight.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the ship displaces enough water for buoyant force to support its weight, or that its average density is less than water.

modelAnswer: A stone is denser than water, so the upthrust on it is less than its weight and it sinks.
A ship is hollow and has a large volume, so it displaces enough water for the buoyant force to balance its weight; its average density is less than that of water.

items.followUp: Why do coastal areas usually have a smaller daily temperature change than deserts?

rubric.why: The material in a desert, especially sand, heats and cools quickly because of its low specific heat capacity.
rubric.description: Explains rapid heating during the day
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the desert’s rapid heating to the low specific heat capacity of sand or the ground.

rubric.why: The same low specific heat capacity means the ground loses heat quickly after sunset.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the desert ground cools or loses heat quickly after sunset due to its low specific heat capacity.

modelAnswer: Desert sand has a low specific heat capacity, so it heats up quickly during the day.
After sunset, it also loses heat quickly and cools rapidly.

items.followUp: State two arrangements that help a bus remain stable.

rubric.why: A low centre of gravity makes it less likely that the line of action of the weight will pass outside the base.
rubric.description: States that the centre of gravity should be low
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a low centre of gravity.

rubric.why: A broad base gives the vehicle a wider range over which its weight can act without toppling.
rubric.description: States that the base should be broad
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a broad or wide base.

modelAnswer: A vehicle is made more stable by keeping its centre of gravity low.
It is also provided with a broad base.

items.followUp: Define unlike parallel forces and give an example.

rubric.why: Like parallel forces have parallel lines of action and act in the same direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the forces are parallel and act in the same direction.

rubric.why: A valid example must show two forces that are parallel and act in the same direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable example, such as two people pushing a car in the same direction or parallel weights acting downward.

modelAnswer: Like parallel forces are forces whose lines of action are parallel and which act in the same direction.
Example: two people pushing a car in the same direction exert like parallel forces.
